reviews.text: Game is very fun and addicting! I found it hard at first but the more I played the more I unlocked to make runs easier and get further into the harder levels. Really fun so far, especially if you like a chill but engaging experience :)
Really fun game! The graphics are probably the best part I think. Still trying to make it to level 3!

In the best way, this is reminiscent of those immensely addictive games you'd get on a PS1 demo disc with the looping (earworm worthy) music, a unique but not overbearing art style and productivity destroying gameplay loop. Progress on upgrades is fairly slow, but that gives you time to learn some of the cards (which serve to keep that slow progress interesting). Scratches the deckbuilder itch, whilst also helping to atone for all those 2ps lost in the arcade.

Very enjoyable, pretty addicting gameplay loop, I found myself wanting to get the upgrades for the Trinkets and the grind was fun! I've made it to the 4th machine once so far in around 5 hours which felt rewarding but after a while I found myself wanting to get back, with no luck so far. I do think the 2nd machine is a bit hard, specifically the spinning bit in the centre of the backboard stopping Euphoria build up and I think a bug where the coins get stuck in the side chutes during Euphoria. Overall very enjoyable for the first EA release and looking forward to potential updates!

DO NOT BUY. Not sure what they have done but the tutorial starts off at needing 600 points to progress with 25 coins. Coins get stuck everywhere and you can literally do nothing but drop more. They have no support and good luck if you need to go back through the tutorial, there is nothing that gives you an explanation on how to play.
The game does a great job of making you feel powerful. As your deck grows, so does the scale of the explosions.
The "godly combos" are no joke! When you finally align your deck perfectly, the resulting cascade is glorious.
The elemental synergies are brilliantly designed. Mixing fireballs with windy blasts creates some truly wild screen-clearing effects.
The Cascadier offers a unique twist on the deckbuilding genre. Dropping charged coins into magical machines creates such explosive visuals.
Game needs balance before it will be fair. I am not able to reliably beat the second or third rounds and the game requires heavy grinding for upgrades. A disappointing coin pusher without substance.
